summary: A completed target-level planning pass for the classical residue map, importing its four existing canonical targets rather than duplicating them. Adds the canonical unit-part API and the characterization by unit-unit vanishing and mixed normalization. The reader supplies all target contracts, discriminating tests, complete elementary proof cases and exact Milnor/classical descent boundaries. The elementary pairing is source-decomposed; classical K₂ transport retains the existing stable-colimit and ordinary-presentation dependencies of the infinite-field Matsumoto proof.

nodes.title: The unit part relative to a uniformizer
nodes.statement: For a commutative field F, a valuation v:F→ℤᵐ⁰, and t∈Fˣ with ord_v(t)=1, define unitPart(v,t,f)=f·t^(−ord_v(f)) for every f∈Fˣ, as an element of the existing subgroup v.valuationSubring.unitGroup. It has order zero and f=t^ord_v(f)·unitPart(v,t,f); this property uniquely determines it. No residue is taken in this definition.
hypotheses: v has integer multiplicative values; t is a field unit of order one. Surjectivity need not be supplied separately for this definition.
f is a field unit, so the junk order at zero is never used.
proofSteps: Use Valuation.ord_mul and ord_zpow to compute ord(f·t^(−ord(f)))=ord(f)−ord(f)=0. Then valuation_eq_exp_neg_ord and Valuation.mem_unitGroup_iff package the field unit in the existing subgroup.
Cancellation gives the decomposition and uniqueness. Multiplication, inversion and integer powers follow by order arithmetic in the commutative field unit group.
Every existing valuation-subring unit has valuation one and hence order zero; this proves the compatibility API without adding another unit type.
For t′=tε expand (tε)^(−ord(f)); commutativity gives the parameter-change formula. It is an equality of subring units, not just of their residues.
acceptance: All eleven API statements and five tests below hold on the existing carriers.
Changing a uniformizer changes the unit part exactly by the displayed unit power; the unit part itself is not parameter-independent.

uses.how: Provide canonical subring-unit inputs to the residue map and show cancellation of the parameter change.
Expand both inputs into an integer power and a unit to determine every normalized Steinberg pairing.
The source proof decomposes both symbol entries into a uniformizer power and a unit; this API packages exactly that operation.

api.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.unitPart
api.statement: For t∈Fˣ with ord(t)=1 and f∈Fˣ, unitPart(v,t,f)=f·t^(−ord(f)), packaged in v.valuationSubring.unitGroup.

api.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.coe_unitPart
api.statement: The underlying field unit of unitPart(v,t,f) is f·t^(−ord(f)).

api.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.unitPart_eq_iff
api.statement: For w in the valuation-subring unit subgroup, unitPart(v,t,f)=w iff f=t^ord(f)·w.

api.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.unitPart_of_unit
api.statement: For w in the existing valuation-subring unit subgroup, unitPart(v,t,w)=w. In particular this holds after transporting an Rˣ element by unitGroupMulEquiv.symm.

api.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.unitPart_zpow
api.statement: For every integer n, unitPart(v,t,f^n)=unitPart(v,t,f)^n, including negative n.

api.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.unitPart_change
api.statement: If t′=tε for ε in the valuation-subring unit subgroup, then unitPart(v,t′,f)=unitPart(v,t,f)·ε^(−ord(f)).

tests.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.unitPart_unit_compatibility
tests.statement: For w∈Rˣ, unitPart applied to the ambient field unit of unitGroupMulEquiv.symm(w) equals that same subgroup element. This rejects a separate residue-class or quotient carrier.

tests.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.unitPart_negative_power
tests.statement: unitPart(v,t,t^(−2))=1. Using the natural absolute value of the order gives t^(−4), which is not even a unit of the valuation ring.

tests.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.unitPart_five_values
tests.statement: For ℚ at 5 with t=5, the unit parts of 2, 10, and 2/5 are all 2 as rational field units. A constant-one or reduction-only function fails these values.

tests.name: TauCeti.TameSymbol.unitPart_change_five
tests.statement: For ℚ at 5, t′=10 is another order-one parameter and unitPart(v,10,5)=1/2, whereas unitPart(v,5,5)=1.

nodes.title: Characterization of the normalized tame symbol
nodes.statement: Let v be a surjective valuation F→ℤᵐ⁰, t∈Fˣ with ord_v(t)=1, R its valuation ring, k its residue field, and res:Rˣ→kˣ the existing unit residue. If c:Fˣ×Fˣ→kˣ is multiplicative in each variable, satisfies c(a,1−a)=1 for a≠0,1, is one on pairs of R-units, and satisfies c(u,t)=res(u) for every R-unit u, then c(f,g)=tameSymbol(v,f,g) for all field units f,g. Equivalently the descended Milnor homomorphism is uniquely determined by unit-unit vanishing and its values on {u,t}; the classical-K₂ version uses the already owned Matsumoto comparison.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field and v is normalized and surjective. No completeness, finiteness of the residue field or characteristic restriction is imposed.
c takes values in the actual residue-field unit group; complementary inputs are nonzero.
Both the unit-unit and mixed-pair normalizations are required.
proofSteps: Apply the existing field-only sign calculus to c: c(a,−a)=1, c(a,b)=c(b,a)⁻¹ and c(a,a)=c(a,−1). This proof uses bilinearity and the Steinberg relation, not Matsumoto injectivity.
The mixed normalization gives c(−1,t)=−1 in kˣ; skew-symmetry and (−1)⁻¹=−1 give c(t,−1)=−1 and c(t,t)=−1. For each R-unit w it also gives c(t,w)=res(w)⁻¹.

Write f=t^a u and g=t^b w using unitPart. Expand by bilinearity for all integer exponents: c(f,g)=c(t,t)^(ab)c(t,w)^a c(u,t)^b c(u,w). Substitute the normalizations to obtain (−1)^(ab)res(u)^b res(w)^(−a).

This is exactly the inherited tameSymbol formula. Function extensionality proves equality of pairings. The tensor universal property and symbol homomorphism extensionality give the Milnor corollary; compose with the imported Matsumoto equivalence for the classical corollary.
acceptance: The constant-one pairing fails c(2,5)=2 over ℚ at 5.
The inverse K-book pairing fails the same normalization since it sends (2,5) to 3.
The unsigned formula satisfies the mixed values but fails the Steinberg hypothesis on (1/5,4/5), where it is 4 rather than 1 at 5.
No claim that all of K₂ is generated solely by {u,t} is used: pairs of ring units are killed only after applying this homomorphism.

gaps.title: Inherited classical-K₂ comparison boundary
gaps.detail: Only the classical-K₂ transport and classical uniqueness corollary require these inherited open inputs: G-stable-witness in the accepted T.2-symbols packet, ultimately T.1 G-colimit, and that packet’s exact ReductiveGroups Layer 7 ordinary root-presentation/Bruhat-coordinate API request. The degree-two tensor universal property and homogeneous-components comparison already have exact T.2-symbols nodes. No new K₂ carrier or foundational presentation is planned here. Surjectivity of a discrete valuation forces F infinite, by the distinct orders of t^n; the finite-field Matsumoto proof gap and arithmetic Bass–Tate gap are consequently outside this stage.

closureLedger.conclusion: The actual subgroup-valued unit part and residue homomorphism give the signed pairing; no completeness assumption.
The order-zero product gives a parameter-free expression; alternatively parameter-change exponents cancel.
Both bilinear laws and all four Steinberg cases are written in the reader.
Milnor descent and surjectivity use exact imported presentation nodes; classical transport retains the single recorded inherited boundary.
